title: Sensor Spike Count
description: A sensor logs readings `a` in time order. A spike is a reading that differs from the previous reading by more than `t` (in either direction). Return the number of spikes (the first reading cannot be a spike).

title: Longest Flat Plateau
description: Return the length of the longest block of consecutive readings in `a` that are all equal.

title: Best Window Average
description: Return the largest value of `floor(sum / k)` over all windows of `k` consecutive readings of `a`.

title: Fill Dropouts Total
description: A sensor reports `-1` when a reading is lost. Every lost reading is replaced by the most recent valid reading before it (`0` if there is none). Return the sum of the readings after replacement.

examples.explanation: The completed readings add up to 14.
The completed readings add up to 0.

title: Clamped Reading Sum
description: Every reading is limited to the range `[lo, hi]`: values below `lo` become `lo` and values above `hi` become `hi`. Return the sum of the limited readings.

title: Readings In Band
description: Return how many readings of `a` lie in the inclusive range `[lo, hi]`.
constraints: -1000 <= a[i], lo, hi <= 1000 and lo <= hi

title: Reorder Alerts
description: `stock[i]` is the number of units of product `i` on the shelf and `minimum[i]` is its reorder level. A product needs reordering when its stock is strictly below its reorder level. Return how many products need reordering.

title: Bulk Discount Total
description: A cart has items with unit prices `price[i]` and quantities `qty[i]`. A line with quantity at least `bulkQty` gets `pct` percent off the line total; the discount for a line is rounded down to a whole number. Return the total to pay.

title: Cash Rounding Total
description: A cash register in a country without 1-cent coins rounds the final total (in cents) to the nearest multiple of `5`; a total ending in `2` or `7` rounds down and one ending in `3` or `8` rounds up (so an exact halfway cannot occur). Return the rounded total of all the prices `cents`.

title: Free Shipping Gap
description: A shop gives free shipping when the discounted cart value reaches `threshold`. The cart value is `total` and a discount of `pct` percent is applied, rounded down to a whole number of the discount amount (the discount is `total * pct / 100` rounded down). Return how much more must be added to the original total, before discount, so the discounted value reaches the threshold; return `0` if it already does. The extra amount added is also discounted with the same rule applied to the whole new total.

title: Pair Deal Total
description: A shop runs a pair deal: after sorting the item prices from the highest to the lowest, items are paired up (first with second, third with fourth, ...) and in every pair the cheaper item is free; an unpaired last item is paid in full. Return the total to pay.

title: Inventory Shortfall Total
description: `need[i]` units of product `i` are ordered and `have[i]` units are in stock. Return the total number of units that cannot be supplied, that is the sum of `max(0, need[i] - have[i])`.

title: Shelf Boxes Needed
description: Product `i` has `items[i]` units and they are packed into boxes holding at most `cap` units each (one product per box). Return the total number of boxes needed.

title: Best Coupon Saving
description: A coupon list `coupons` holds flat pairs `(minSpend, off)`: a coupon can be used if the cart `total` is at least `minSpend`, and then reduces the price by `off`. Only one coupon may be used. Return the largest saving possible (`0` if no coupon applies).
constraints: coupons.length is even, at most 2000, and 0 <= minSpend, off <= 100000

title: Mean Without Extremes
description: Remove one lowest and one highest score from `scores` (if a value occurs several times only one copy of it is removed from each end), then return the average of the remaining scores rounded down.

title: Passing Students
description: Return the number of scores in `scores` that are at least `pass`.

title: Curved Scores Total
description: A teacher adds `curve` points to every score, but no score may go above `100` after the curve. Return the sum of the curved scores.

examples.explanation: The curved scores add up to 130.
The curved scores add up to 100.

title: Score Rank
description: Return the rank of the score `s` among `scores`: one plus the number of scores strictly greater than `s` (so equal scores share the same rank). The value `s` need not appear in the list.

title: Median Score Floor
description: Return the median of `scores`: the middle value after sorting when the count is odd, or the average of the two middle values rounded down when the count is even.

title: Average Pace Seconds
description: A runner covers `meters` metres in `seconds` seconds. Return the average pace in whole seconds per kilometre, rounded down.

examples.explanation: The pace is 300 seconds per kilometre.
The pace is 300 seconds per kilometre.

title: Negative Split Check
description: `splits[i]` is the time of the `i`-th kilometre of a race, and the number of kilometres is even. A race is a negative split if the total time of its second half is strictly smaller than the total time of its first half. Return `true` for a negative split.

examples.explanation: The race is a negative split: True.
The race is a negative split: False.

title: Fastest Lap
description: Return the 0-based index of the fastest (smallest) lap time in `laps`; if several laps share the smallest time return the first of them.

examples.explanation: The fastest lap is at index 1.
The fastest lap is at index 0.

title: Medal Table Points
description: A country's medals are given as `gold`, `silver` and `bronze` counts. Gold is worth 3 points, silver 2 and bronze 1. Return the total points.
constraints: All inputs are integers or strings within the stated ranges

title: Size In Largest Unit
description: Write a byte count `b` using the largest unit among `B`, `KB`, `MB`, `GB`, `TB` (each unit is 1024 times the previous one) for which the value is at least 1 (use `B` when `b < 1024`). Round the value down to a whole number and return it directly followed by the unit, for example `2KB`.
constraints: Units: B, KB, MB, GB, TB (TB is the largest)

title: Download Seconds
description: A file of `mb` megabytes is downloaded over a link of `mbps` megabits per second (8 bits make a byte, and the full link speed is used). Return the number of whole seconds the download takes, rounded up.

title: Disk Blocks Used
description: A disk stores each file in whole blocks of `block` bytes; a file of size `s` occupies `ceil(s / block)` blocks (an empty file occupies none). Return the total number of blocks used by the files `sizes`.

title: Duration In Words
description: Write a number of seconds as hours, minutes and seconds in the form `1h 2m 3s`, leaving out every part that is zero (hours are not limited to 23). If the duration is `0` return `0s`.
constraints: Parts are separated by single spaces

title: Rectangle Bounding Area
description: Points are given as flat pairs `pts = [x1, y1, x2, y2, ...]`. Return the area of the smallest axis-aligned rectangle that contains all the points (it is `0` when the points lie on a line parallel to an axis).

title: Points In Quadrant One
description: Points are given as flat pairs `pts = [x1, y1, x2, y2, ...]`. Return how many points have both coordinates strictly positive.

examples.explanation: 1 points lie in the first quadrant.
0 points lie in the first quadrant.

title: Nearest Point Index
description: Points are given as flat pairs `pts = [x1, y1, x2, y2, ...]`. Return the 0-based index of the point with the smallest Manhattan distance `|dx| + |dy|` to `(x, y)`; if several points tie, return the smallest index.

title: Rectangle Overlap Cells
description: Two axis-aligned rectangles on a grid are given by their lower-left and upper-right corners, `(ax1, ay1, ax2, ay2)` and `(bx1, by1, bx2, by2)`, each with `x1 < x2` and `y1 < y2`. They cover the unit cells strictly between those corners. Return the number of unit cells covered by both rectangles.
constraints: x1 < x2 and y1 < y2 for each rectangle

title: Late Fee Total
description: Books are returned `daysLate[i]` days after their due date (`0` or less means on time). A book that is late costs `fee` per late day, but the fee for one book never exceeds `cap`. Return the total of all fees.

title: Books Due Today
description: Each loan has a start day `start[i]` and a loan length `length[i]` in days, so the book is due on day `start[i] + length[i]`. Return how many books are due on day `today`.

title: Longest Overdue
description: Each loan is due on day `due[i]` and was returned on day `back[i]`. Return the largest number of days any book was overdue, or `0` if no book was returned after its due day.

examples.explanation: The longest overdue period is 2 days.
The longest overdue period is 0 days.

title: Renewals Allowed
description: A library book is borrowed for `base` days and may be renewed up to `maxRenewals` times, each renewal adding `extra` days. A reader wants to keep the book for `need` days in a row (counting from the first day it is borrowed). Return the smallest number of renewals needed, or `-1` if even the maximum number of renewals is not enough.

examples.explanation: The number of renewals needed is 1 (-1 means impossible).
The number of renewals needed is 0 (-1 means impossible).

title: Peaks With Prominence
description: A peak is an index `i` with `0 < i < n-1` and `a[i] > a[i-1]` and `a[i] > a[i+1]`. Its prominence is measured like this: walk left from the peak until you reach a value strictly higher than `a[i]` (or the left end) and remember the lowest value seen on the way, including `a[i]` itself; do the same to the right; the prominence is `a[i]` minus the larger of the two lowest values. Return how many peaks have prominence at least `p`.

title: Hysteresis Alarm Count
description: An alarm is off at the start. While it is off, a reading that is at least `hi` switches it on. While it is on, a reading that is at most `lo` switches it off. Other readings change nothing. Return how many times the alarm switches on while processing `a` in order.

title: Debounced Button Presses
description: A button is sampled every millisecond and `a` holds the samples (`1` pressed, `0` released). Electrical noise is filtered by counting a press only after the signal has been `1` for `k` samples in a row; one long block of ones counts at most once, no matter how long it lasts. Return the number of presses counted.

title: Calibration Table Lookup
description: A sensor is calibrated with a table: raw readings `xs` (strictly increasing) map to calibrated values `ys`. For a raw reading `q` between two table entries the calibrated value lies on the straight line between them, rounded down to a whole number (towards negative infinity). A reading at or below the first entry gives the first calibrated value and one at or above the last entry gives the last one. Return the calibrated value for `q`.
constraints: 1 <= xs.length = ys.length <= 100000 and xs is strictly increasing

title: Longest Steady Stretch
description: A stretch of readings is steady if its largest and smallest values differ by at most `t`. Return the length of the longest steady stretch of consecutive readings in `a`.

examples.explanation: The longest steady stretch has 2 readings.
The longest steady stretch has 1 readings.

title: Rate Limiter Allowed Requests
description: A rate limiter allows at most `L` requests in any window of `W` seconds. Requests arrive at the times `ts` (whole seconds, non-decreasing). A request at time `t` is allowed if fewer than `L` already allowed requests have times in `(t - W, t]`; otherwise it is rejected, and rejected requests are not counted towards later limits. Return the number of allowed requests.
constraints: 1 <= ts.length <= 100000 and ts is non-decreasing, 0 <= ts[i] <= 1000000000

title: Batch Flush Count
description: Events arrive at the times `ts` (whole seconds, non-decreasing) and are collected in a buffer. The buffer is flushed (emptied) as soon as it holds `S` events, or when the oldest event in it has waited `T` seconds, that is at time `first + T` (a timeout flush happens before any event that arrives at that same second is added). Whatever is still in the buffer after the last event is flushed once more at the timeout. Return the total number of flushes.
constraints: 1 <= ts.length <= 100000 and ts is non-decreasing, 0 <= ts[i] <= 1000000000

title: Diverse Windows Count
description: Return the number of windows of `k` consecutive elements of `a` that contain at least `m` different values.

title: Longest Session Span
description: User events happen at the times `ts` (sorted, non-decreasing). Consecutive events belong to the same session if the gap between them is at most `g`; a larger gap starts a new session. The span of a session is its last event time minus its first event time. Return the largest span of any session.

examples.explanation: The longest session spans 2 time units.
The longest session spans 0 time units.

title: Constant Offset Correction Error
description: A sensor reads `a[i]` where the true value is `b[i]`. You may add one integer constant `c` to every reading. Return the smallest possible value of the total error `sum |a[i] + c - b[i]|`.

title: Markup Nesting Depth
description: `s` is a sequence of tags: an opening tag `<name>` or a closing tag `</name>`, where `name` is 1 to 5 lowercase letters and there is no text in between. The sequence is well formed if every closing tag closes the most recently opened tag that is still open, and no tag stays open at the end. Return the largest number of tags that are open at the same time in a well-formed sequence, or `-1` if the sequence is not well formed.

examples.explanation: The nesting depth is 1 (-1 means malformed).
The nesting depth is 2 (-1 means malformed).

constraints: s is a concatenation of tags <name> and </name> with 1 to 5 lowercase letters

title: CSV Field Count
description: A line of comma-separated values is given in `s`. A field may be wrapped in double quotes; inside a quoted field commas are ordinary characters and a double quote is written as two double quotes in a row. A comma outside quotes ends a field. Return the number of fields in the line (an empty line, or a line made of nothing, has one empty field).
constraints: the quoting in s is valid: a quote opens a field only at its start and every quoted field is closed

title: JSON Nesting Depth
description: `s` is a valid JSON text. Arrays `[...]` and objects `{...}` can be nested inside each other, and strings may contain brackets, braces, escaped quotes and backslashes that are just text. Return the deepest nesting level of arrays and objects (`0` for a text with no array or object, `1` for a flat array or object, and so on).
constraints: s is valid JSON; strings use the standard escapes

title: Minimum Line Diff Size
description: Two versions of a file are given as lists of lines, each line a lowercase word and the lines separated by `|`. A diff turns the first file into the second by deleting some lines and inserting others; every deleted line and every inserted line costs `1`, and lines that stay keep their relative order. Return the smallest possible total cost.
constraints: 1 <= number of lines in a, b <= 1000
each line is 1 to 10 lowercase letters

title: Spell Check Close Words
description: `words` is a dictionary of lowercase words separated by single spaces. Return how many dictionary words are within edit distance `1` of `w` (equal to it, or reachable by inserting, deleting or replacing exactly one letter).

examples.input: w = "cat", words = "cat bat cut cart at"
examples.explanation: 5 dictionary words are within one edit.
4 dictionary words are within one edit.

constraints: w and every word are 1 to 20 lowercase letters

title: Macro Expansion Length
description: A grammar is given as `rules`, a list of definitions separated by `;`, each of the form `X=body` where `X` is an uppercase letter and `body` is a string of uppercase letters (symbols to expand further) and lowercase letters (plain text). Every uppercase letter used is defined exactly once and expanding never loops forever. Starting from `A`, repeatedly replace every uppercase letter by its body until only lowercase letters remain. Return the length of the final text modulo `1000000007`.

examples.explanation: The expanded text has 1 letters modulo 1000000007.
The expanded text has 4 letters modulo 1000000007.

constraints: 1 <= number of rules <= 26, each body has 1 to 10 letters
the rules contain a definition of A and are acyclic

title: Run-Length Strings Equal
description: A run-length string is a list of items, each a lowercase letter followed by a positive repeat count (written without leading zeros), such as `a3b2` meaning `aaabb`. The same text can be written in several ways (`a2a1` and `a3` mean the same). Return `true` if the texts described by `a` and `b` are identical.

examples.explanation: The decoded texts are equal: True.
The decoded texts are equal: True.

title: Distinct Phone Numbers
description: `s` is a list of phone numbers separated by `;`, each written with arbitrary digits and punctuation (spaces, dashes, brackets, plus signs). To compare numbers, remove every character that is not a digit; if that leaves 11 digits and the first one is `1`, drop the first digit (a country code). A number is valid if exactly 10 digits remain. Return the number of different valid numbers.
constraints: the numbers contain digits, spaces, dashes, brackets and plus signs

title: Cron Minute Field Matches
description: A cron minute field is a comma-separated list of items matched against the minutes `0..59`. An item is `*` (every minute), a number `n`, a range `a-b` (all minutes from `a` to `b` inclusive), or any of these followed by `/s`: with `*/s` or `a-b/s` it takes every `s`-th minute counting from the start of the range (`*` starts at `0`), and `n/s` means every `s`-th minute from `n` up to `59`. A minute matches if any item matches it. Return the number of matching minutes.
constraints: numbers are at most 59, steps are at least 1, and in a range a <= b

title: Falling Stones Row Total
description: A grid is stored row by row in `g` with `cols` cells per row; row `0` is the top. A cell holds `0` (empty), `1` (a stone) or `2` (a fixed block). Gravity pulls every stone straight down until it rests on the bottom edge, on a fixed block, or on another stone that has already come to rest. Fixed blocks never move. Return the sum of the row numbers of all stones after everything has settled.

examples.explanation: The stones' row numbers add up to 1.
The stones' row numbers add up to 2.

constraints: g.length is a multiple of cols and every g[i] is 0, 1 or 2

title: Paint Bucket Replay
description: An image is stored row by row in `g` with `cols` pixels per row, each pixel a colour number. `ops` is a flat list of triples `(row, column, colour)`. Each operation is a paint bucket: the connected region (sharing edges, not corners) of pixels with the same colour as the clicked pixel is repainted with the new colour; nothing happens if the clicked pixel already has the new colour. Return how many pixels have colour `1` after all operations.

examples.explanation: 0 pixels have colour 1 at the end.
4 pixels have colour 1 at the end.

constraints: 1 <= cols <= 100 and 1 <= g.length <= 10000, g.length is a multiple of cols
0 <= g[i], colour <= 100 and 1 <= number of operations <= 1000 with valid pixel positions

title: Pipe Network Reach
description: A grid of pipe pieces is stored row by row in `g` with `cols` pieces per row. Each piece is a number from `0` to `15` whose bits say which sides are open: bit `0` (value 1) is the top side, bit `1` (value 2) the right side, bit `2` (value 4) the bottom side and bit `3` (value 8) the left side. Water passes between two neighbouring cells only if both pieces are open towards each other. Water enters at the cell `start`. Return the number of cells (including the start cell) that the water can reach.
constraints: 1 <= cols <= 100 and 1 <= g.length <= 10000, g.length is a multiple of cols

title: Conveyor Belt Exit Steps
description: A factory floor is stored row by row in `g` with `cols` cells per row. Every cell is a conveyor belt pointing in one direction: `0` up, `1` right, `2` down, `3` left (row `0` is the top). A parcel placed on the cell `start` moves one cell per step in the direction of the belt it is on. Return the number of steps until the parcel leaves the grid (the step that carries it off the edge counts), or `-1` if it never leaves.

examples.explanation: The parcel leaves after 1 steps (-1 means never).
The parcel leaves after 2 steps (-1 means never).

constraints: 1 <= cols <= 100 and 1 <= g.length <= 10000, g.length is a multiple of cols

title: Minesweeper Reveal Count
description: A minefield is stored row by row in `g` with `cols` cells per row (`1` is a mine, `0` is safe). The player clicks the safe cell `start`. The clicked cell is revealed; whenever a revealed cell has no mines among its 8 neighbours, all of its neighbours are revealed too, and so on. Return the number of revealed cells.
constraints: 1 <= cols <= 100 and 1 <= g.length <= 10000, g.length is a multiple of cols
every g[i] is 0 or 1 and g[start] = 0

title: Sandpile Topple Count
description: A grid of grain piles is stored row by row in `g` with `cols` piles per row. Whenever a pile holds `4` or more grains it topples: it loses `4` grains and each of its up to four edge-neighbours gains one grain (grains that would leave the grid are lost). Toppling continues, in any order, until every pile holds at most `3` grains; the number of topplings does not depend on the order. Return the total number of topplings.
constraints: 1 <= cols <= 50 and 1 <= g.length <= 2500, g.length is a multiple of cols

title: Langton Ant Black Cells
description: An ant walks on an infinite grid whose cells are all white at the start. It starts on some cell facing north. In each step: on a white cell the ant turns 90 degrees right, turns that cell black and moves one cell forward; on a black cell it turns 90 degrees left, turns that cell white and moves one cell forward. Return the number of black cells after `N` steps.

examples.explanation: After N steps 0 cells are black.
After N steps 1 cells are black.

title: Turing Machine Halt Steps
description: A Turing machine has `k` states numbered `0..k-1` and works on an infinite tape of cells holding `0` or `1` (all `0` at the start). It starts in state `0` with its head on some cell. `table` lists, for each state in order and for each symbol `0` then `1` under the head, a triple `(write, move, next)`: write that symbol, move the head by `move` (`-1` left or `+1` right), and go to state `next`; the value `next = -1` means the machine halts after this step. Return the number of steps executed when it halts, or `-1` if it has not halted after `10000` steps.

examples.explanation: The machine halts after 1 steps (-1 means it did not halt).
The machine halts after -1 steps (-1 means it did not halt).

constraints: write is 0 or 1, move is -1 or 1, next is -1 or a valid state

title: Rolling Die Top Face
description: A standard die starts on a table with `1` on top, `6` on the bottom, `2` facing north, `5` facing south, `3` facing east and `4` facing west. The string `s` rolls the die one square at a time without slipping: `N` rolls it north, `S` south, `E` east and `W` west. Return the number on the top face at the end.
constraints: s consists of N, S, E and W

title: Billiard Wall Bounces
description: A ball is shot from the bottom-left corner of a `w x h` rectangular table at 45 degrees, so it moves one unit right and one unit up each time step. Whenever it hits a side it bounces perfectly (the angle stays 45 degrees). It stops as soon as it reaches any corner. Return the number of times it bounced off a side before reaching that corner.

examples.explanation: The ball bounces 0 times before reaching a corner.
The ball bounces 1 times before reaching a corner.

constraints: The ball starts exactly in a corner and moves diagonally

title: Pairwise AND Popcount Sum
description: For every pair of indices `i < j`, count the number of `1` bits in `a[i] AND a[j]`. Return the sum of these counts over all pairs, modulo `1000000007`.

examples.explanation: The popcounts add up to 0 modulo 1000000007.
The popcounts add up to 2 modulo 1000000007.

title: All Subsets XOR Total
description: The XOR of an empty collection is `0`. Consider every subset of the positions of `a` (there are `2^n` of them, including the empty one) and take the XOR of the chosen values. Return the sum of these XOR values over all subsets, modulo `1000000007`.

examples.explanation: The subset XOR values add up to 1 modulo 1000000007.
The subset XOR values add up to 2 modulo 1000000007.

title: Perfect Square Pair Count
description: Return the number of pairs of indices `i < j` such that `a[i] + a[j]` is a perfect square (`0, 1, 4, 9, ...`).

examples.explanation: 1 pairs add up to a perfect square.
0 pairs add up to a perfect square.

title: D'Hondt Seat Allocation
description: In the D'Hondt method seats are given one at a time: each seat goes to the party with the largest quotient `votes / (seats already won + 1)`. If quotients are equal, the party with more votes gets the seat, and if that ties too, the party with the smaller index. Return how many of the `seats` seats party `p` receives.

title: Largest Remainder Seats
description: In the largest remainder method a party first gets `floor(votes * seats / totalVotes)` seats. The seats that are still unassigned are then given one each to the parties with the largest remainders `(votes * seats) mod totalVotes`, ties going to the smaller party index. If nobody has any votes, every party gets `0` seats. Return the number of seats party `p` gets.

title: Badminton Match Winner
description: A badminton match is the best of three games. `s` lists the winner of each rally (`A` or `B`) in order. A game is won by the first side to reach `21` points with a lead of at least `2`; if the score reaches `29-29` the side that reaches `30` points wins at once. Every new game starts at `0-0` and the match ends as soon as one side has won two games (rallies after that are ignored). Return `A` or `B` for the winner of the match, or `none` if the rallies given do not finish the match.
constraints: s consists of A and B

title: Table Tennis Serves By A
description: In table tennis player `A` serves the first rally. The serve changes after every 2 rallies played, until both players have at least 10 points; from then on the serve changes after every single rally (the server of a rally is decided by the number `t` of rallies already played: when both have at least 10 points, `A` serves if `t` is even and `B` if `t` is odd). `s` lists the winner of each rally (`A` or `B`) in order; ignore when the game would normally end. Return how many of the rallies in `s` were served by `A`.
constraints: s consists of A and B

title: Shortest Odd Cycle Length
description: An undirected graph has `n` nodes `0..n-1` and edges given as flat pairs `edges`. A cycle visits `k >= 3` different nodes, returns to the first one, and uses `k` distinct edges; it is odd if `k` is odd. Return the length of the shortest odd cycle, or `-1` if the graph has no odd cycle (it is bipartite).

examples.explanation: The shortest odd cycle has length 3 (-1 means none).
The shortest odd cycle has length -1 (-1 means none).

constraints: 1 <= n <= 1000 and edges.length is even with at most 5000 edges
0 <= a, b < n, a != b and no edge is listed twice

title: Articulation Point Count
description: An undirected graph has `n` nodes `0..n-1` (it may be disconnected) and edges given as flat pairs `edges`. A node is an articulation point if removing it, together with its edges, increases the number of connected components of the graph. Return the number of articulation points.
constraints: 1 <= n <= 100000 and edges.length is even with at most 200000 edges
0 <= a, b < n and a != b; parallel edges may appear

title: Divisible Substrings Count
description: `s` is a string of decimal digits. Return the number of non-empty substrings (counted by position, so equal substrings at different positions count separately) whose value, read as a decimal number, is divisible by `k`. A substring with leading zeros is read normally (`007` is `7`, `000` is `0`).

title: Months To Savings Goal
description: You save `d` coins in the first month, and every following month you save `r` coins more than in the month before (`d, d + r, d + 2r, ...`). Return the smallest number of months after which your total savings are at least `goal`, or `-1` if that never happens. If `goal` is `0` or less the answer is `0`.

examples.explanation: You reach the goal after 4 months (-1 means never).
You reach the goal after -1 months (-1 means never).

title: Labeled Trees With Given Degrees
description: A tree on `n` labelled nodes `0..n-1` has `n - 1` edges and is connected. Return the number of different labelled trees in which node `i` has exactly `deg[i]` neighbours, modulo `1000000007`. Two trees are different if their edge sets differ. A single node has degree `0` and counts as one tree.

title: Inversions Over All Rotations
description: An inversion of an array is a pair of positions `i < j` with `b[i] > b[j]`. Rotating the array `a` left by `k` moves its first `k` elements to the end. Return the sum, over all `n` rotations (`k = 0, 1, ..., n - 1`), of the number of inversions of the rotated array, modulo `1000000007`.

examples.explanation: The inversions of all rotations add up to 0 modulo 1000000007.
The inversions of all rotations add up to 1 modulo 1000000007.

title: Longest Palindromic Subsequence With Changes
description: You may change at most `k` characters of the string `s` to any lowercase letters. After the changes, look at the longest palindromic subsequence (a subsequence that reads the same forwards and backwards). Return the largest length of such a subsequence that can be reached.

examples.explanation: The longest palindromic subsequence can reach length 1.
The longest palindromic subsequence can reach length 3.

title: Longest Approximate Repeat
description: Look for two different starting positions `i < j` in `s` and a length `L` such that the substrings `s[i..i+L-1]` and `s[j..j+L-1]` (the two may overlap) differ in at most `k` positions. Return the largest such `L`, or `0` if there is none (for example when `s` has one character).

examples.explanation: The longest approximate repeat has length 0.
The longest approximate repeat has length 1.

title: Collinear Triples Count
description: Points are given as flat pairs `pts = [x1, y1, x2, y2, ...]` and all points are different. Return the number of triples of points (as sets of three indices) that lie on one straight line.
constraints: -1000000 <= coordinates <= 1000000 and all points are distinct

title: Isosceles Triangle Count
description: Points are given as flat pairs `pts = [x1, y1, x2, y2, ...]` and all points are different. Return the number of triangles, formed by three of the points, that are isosceles (at least two sides of equal length) and non-degenerate (the three points are not on one line).
constraints: -100000 <= coordinates <= 100000 and all points are distinct

title: Divisors Of Factorial Count
description: Return the number of positive divisors of `n!` (the product `1 * 2 * ... * n`), modulo `1000000007`.

title: Ballot Sequences Count
description: In an election candidate A gets `a` votes and candidate B gets `b` votes, counted one by one in some order. Return the number of different orders (sequences of `a` letters `A` and `b` letters `B`) in which A is never behind B at any moment of the count (ties are allowed), modulo `1000000007`.

examples.explanation: There are 1 valid counting orders modulo 1000000007.
There are 1 valid counting orders modulo 1000000007.

constraints: The sequence has a + b votes

title: Tree Isomorphism Check
description: Two trees are given by parent arrays. In `p1` (and in `p2`) node `i + 1` is joined to node `p[i]`, where `p[i] <= i`. The trees have `p1.length + 1` and `p2.length + 1` nodes. Return `true` if the two trees are isomorphic as unrooted trees, that is if the nodes of one can be renamed so that its edges become exactly the edges of the other.

title: Sum Of Subset Ranges
description: The range of a non-empty set of numbers is its largest value minus its smallest value. Consider every non-empty subset of the positions of `a` (positions are different even when values are equal). Return the sum of the ranges of all these subsets, modulo `1000000007`.

examples.explanation: The ranges add up to 0 modulo 1000000007.
The ranges add up to 1 modulo 1000000007.

title: Kth Binary String With Fixed Ones
description: Consider all binary strings of length `n` that contain exactly `m` ones, sorted in dictionary order (`0` comes before `1`). Return the `k`-th string of this list, counting from `1`.

title: Interleaving Ways Count
description: A string `c` is an interleaving of `a` and `b` if its characters can be split into two groups by position so that reading the first group in order gives `a` and reading the second group in order gives `b`. Return the number of different ways to choose the positions of `c` that belong to `a` (two ways are different if the sets of positions differ), modulo `1000000007`. If `c` is not an interleaving, the answer is `0`.
constraints: a, b and c consist of lowercase letters

title: Shortest Window Containing Subsequence
description: Return the length of the shortest contiguous substring of `s` that contains `t` as a subsequence (the letters of `t` appear in it in order, with other letters allowed in between), or `-1` if no such substring exists.

examples.explanation: The shortest window has length 4 (-1 means none).
The shortest window has length 1 (-1 means none).

constraints: s and t consist of lowercase letters

title: Minimum Vertex Cover In Bipartite Graph
description: A bipartite graph has `nl` nodes on the left (numbered `0..nl-1`) and `nr` nodes on the right (numbered `0..nr-1`). `edges` lists flat pairs `(u, v)` with `u` on the left and `v` on the right. A vertex cover is a set of nodes such that every edge has at least one endpoint in the set. Return the smallest possible size of a vertex cover.

examples.explanation: The smallest vertex cover has 0 nodes.
The smallest vertex cover has 1 nodes.

constraints: 1 <= nl, nr <= 1000 and edges.length is even with at most 5000 edges
0 <= u < nl, 0 <= v < nr and no edge is repeated

title: Strings With Exact Letters No Repeats
description: Count the strings of length `n` over an alphabet of `m` letters in which no two neighbouring characters are equal and exactly `k` different letters occur. Return the count modulo `1000000007`.

title: Binary Grid Without Filled Square
description: Fill every cell of an `R x C` grid with `0` or `1`. A filling is allowed if it contains no `2 x 2` block of four neighbouring cells that are all `1`. Return the number of allowed fillings modulo `1000000007`.

title: Lucky Ticket Count
description: A ticket has `2n` digits written in base `base` (digits `0..base-1`, leading zeros allowed). It is lucky if the sum of its first `n` digits equals the sum of its last `n` digits. Return the number of lucky tickets, modulo `1000000007`.

title: Tree Diameter Path Count
description: A tree has nodes `0..n-1` with `n = par.length + 1`; node `i + 1` is joined to node `par[i]` (with `par[i] <= i`). The diameter is the largest number of edges on a path between two nodes. Return the number of unordered pairs of nodes whose path has exactly that many edges, modulo `1000000007`.

examples.explanation: 1 pairs of nodes realise the diameter, modulo 1000000007.
1 pairs of nodes realise the diameter, modulo 1000000007.

title: Zigzag Permutation Count
description: A permutation `p` of `1..n` is a zigzag if `p[0] < p[1] > p[2] < p[3] > ...`, that is the first step goes up and then steps alternate between down and up. Return the number of zigzag permutations of `1..n`, modulo `1000000007`.
constraints: The first step of the zigzag goes up

title: Tree Eccentricity Sum
description: A tree has nodes `0..n-1` with `n = par.length + 1`; node `i + 1` is joined to node `par[i]` (with `par[i] <= i`). The eccentricity of a node is the largest distance (number of edges) from it to any other node. Return the sum of the eccentricities of all nodes, modulo `1000000007`.

examples.explanation: The eccentricities add up to 2 modulo 1000000007.
The eccentricities add up to 5 modulo 1000000007.

title: Window Inversions Total
description: An inversion in a window is a pair of positions `i < j` inside it with `w[i] > w[j]`. Slide a window of `k` consecutive elements over `a` from left to right. Return the sum, over all windows, of the number of inversions inside the window, modulo `1000000007`.

examples.explanation: The window inversions add up to 0 modulo 1000000007.
The window inversions add up to 3 modulo 1000000007.

title: Distinct Values Query Total
description: `queries` lists flat pairs `(l, r)` meaning the part of `a` from index `l` to index `r`, both included. For every query count the number of different values in that part. Return the sum of these counts over all queries, modulo `1000000007`.

examples.explanation: The distinct counts add up to 1 modulo 1000000007.
The distinct counts add up to 1 modulo 1000000007.

title: Best Subarray XOR With Length Limit
description: Consider every non-empty contiguous part of `a` that has at most `L` elements, and take the XOR of its elements. Return the largest XOR value obtained.

title: Kth Smallest Pairwise XOR
description: Consider the XOR `a[i] XOR a[j]` of every pair of positions `i < j`, and sort these `n(n-1)/2` values in non-decreasing order. Return the `k`-th value of the sorted list, counting from `1`.

examples.explanation: The k-th smallest pairwise XOR is 3.
The k-th smallest pairwise XOR is 0.

title: Best Spaced Picks
description: Choose at most `K` positions of `w` such that any two chosen positions are at least `d` apart (their indices differ by at least `d`). Return the largest possible sum of the chosen values (choosing nothing gives `0`; values may be negative).
